goldens.comment: The findMembers() call is now asynchronous and unhandled. The controller may not have member data immediately available, creating a race condition.

In the next action, capping the next offset at user_count can produce an empty page (e.g., total equal to limit results in offset == total, showing 2/2 with no members). This can cause confusing UX on the last page.
The remove_member test uses xhr :put to call the remove_member action, but the route defines delete 'members' => 'groups#remove_member' requiring DELETE method.

The `totalPages` calculation using `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` produces an extra page when `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit`, leading to incorrect pagination. For example, with 100 users and a limit of 50, it reports 3 pages instead of 2, allowing navigation to an empty page.
Expected to return a value at the end of function - code paths without explicit returns will return undefined

The route provides the group's ID in params[:id], but the code attempts to read it from params[:group_id], causing the action to fail. This results in a broken feature when trying to access group memberships.

adjudication_records.issue_text: offset clamping uses stale user_count before the fetch; user_count initialized to 0 causes offset clamping to 0 even when client wants page >1 after count changes
add_members silently ignores usernames that don't match a user, returning success even when no members were added, giving admin no feedback

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::GroupsController#add_members, the code iterates `usernames.split(",")` and only calls `group.add(user)` when `User.find_by_username(username)` returns a user; non-existent usernames are simply skipped. It then does `if group.save` and renders `success_json`. Since `save` typically returns true even when nothing changed, the endpoint can return success even if zero usernames matched (and thus no members were added), providing no explicit feedback about invalid usernames.

adjudication_records.issue_text: remove_member succeeds even if user_id isn't a member; group.save on unchanged model renders success with no validation that removal occurred

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::GroupsController#remove_member, the code does `group.users.delete(user_id)` and then returns success if `group.save` succeeds. It is true that deleting a non-associated user_id is typically a no-op and `group.save` will still return true, so the endpoint will respond with success even if nothing was removed. However, the diff does not establish any requirement that removing a non-member must error; in many APIs DELETE-like operations are intentionally idempotent (success even if the resource/association wasn’t present). The finding asserts a defect (“no validation that removal occurred”) that is not clearly a bug based solely on this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: After adding members, usernames on the controller is never cleared; stale usernames remain in input and can be re-added

adjudication.rationale: In `admin-group.js.es6`, the new `addMembers` action checks `this.get("usernames")` and then calls `this.get("model").addMembers(this.get("usernames"))`, but it never resets/clears `usernames` afterward. The template binds the user-selector input to `usernames` (`{{user-selector usernames=usernames ...}}`), so the entered usernames will remain in the input after the add completes. The code even includes a comment `// TODO: should clear the input`, confirming the behavior is known and currently unimplemented. This makes it possible to submit the same usernames again without retyping (stale input).

adjudication_records.issue_text: addMembers action doesn't pass this context, so success/error handling (e.g. disableSave) is absent

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, the `addMembers` action is defined on the controller and correctly uses `this` as the controller context (`this.get("model").addMembers(...)`). There is no missing binding/`this` context issue shown. Also, `disableSave` is only used to disable the Save button during `save` action; the new `addMembers` flow is separate and there’s no existing mechanism in the diff indicating it should toggle `disableSave` or provide save-like success/error handling. While `addMembers` also doesn’t return the promise or clear the input (noted by TODO), the proposed finding’s claim about context and `disableSave` is not a verifiable defect introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: update allows setting alias_level on automatic groups (only name is guarded), potentially permitting unintended configuration changes to automatic groups

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::GroupsController#update, alias_level is set from params for all groups, including automatic ones. However, the previous implementation (update_put) also set alias_level and visible before checking group.automatic, and only guarded renaming/membership changes. The new code even includes a comment explicitly stating only rename is ignored for automatic groups, and the spec added verifies visible can be changed on an automatic group. So allowing alias_level changes on automatic groups is consistent with prior behavior and appears intentional, not a verifiable defect introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: members endpoint response format changed from plain array to {members: [...], meta: {...}} with no API versioning/compatibility, breaking existing API consumers

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `GroupsController#members` from `render_serialized(members.to_a, GroupUserSerializer)` (a plain JSON array) to `render json: { members: ..., meta: ... }`, i.e., an object wrapper with metadata. This is a concrete, backward-incompatible response format change on an existing endpoint (`/groups/:group_id/members`), and the JS client was updated to match, but any other existing consumers expecting an array would break. No compatibility layer or alternate endpoint/versioning is introduced in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: group.users.count plus group.users.order(...).limit(...) executes two queries; count on large groups can be slow with no caching

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the diff does introduce `total = group.users.count` followed by a separate `group.users.order(...).limit(...).offset(...)` query, so two SQL queries will be issued per request. However, this is a standard/intentional pagination pattern to return both the page of results and `meta.total`. The claim that this is a “real problem” (slow on large groups due to no caching) is performance speculation and not a clear defect/bug introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: removeMember/addMembers in shared model build URLs with /admin/groups/... but findMembers fetches public /groups/...; these methods will fail with 404/403 for non-admin users on user-facing routes; save/destroy similarly call admin endpoints
No test coverage for adding a non-existent username, removing a non-existent/non-member user_id, and removed incremental add/delete test for usernames with trailing spaces or duplicates

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the previous incremental membership update tests that explicitly covered edge cases like adding a non-existent user (and removing non-members) in `context 'incremental'` under `.update`. The new specs add coverage for `add_members` (success + automatic-group rejection) but do not include a test for non-existent usernames (even though `add_members` silently ignores unknown usernames), and the new `remove_member` spec section is incomplete/truncated and does not show coverage for removing a non-existent/non-member `user_id`. The part about trailing spaces/duplicates is not clearly supported by the removed tests, but the broader claim about missing edge-case test coverage after the refactor is verifiable in the diff.
